description: Iconic split-leaf tropical. Thrives in bright indirect light; let soil dry out between waterings.
Nearly indestructible trailing vine. Tolerates low light; water when top inch of soil is dry.
Extremely drought-tolerant upright succulent-like plant. Overwatering is its main enemy.
Elegant white flowers; droops dramatically when thirsty — a built-in reminder.
Fast-growing, produces long runners with baby plantlets. Forgiving of missed waterings.
Glossy leaves, extremely drought-tolerant. Stores water in thick rhizomes.
Statement plant with large violin-shaped leaves. Needs consistent bright light and consistent watering.
Deep burgundy or green glossy leaves. Water when top 2 cm of soil are dry.
Medicinal succulent. Needs very free-draining soil; water deeply then let dry out completely.
Lush arching fronds. Needs consistently moist soil and high humidity.
Striking patterned foliage; one of the most adaptable houseplants.
Tall architectural plant with narrow leaves. Sensitive to fluoride in tap water.
Trailing heart-shaped leaves; very easy to propagate.
Dramatic paddle-shaped leaves. Needs lots of light to eventually produce orange flowers.
Cascading bead-like succulent. Needs excellent drainage; susceptible to root rot.
Long-lived succulent tree-like plant. Water thoroughly; allow to dry fully between waterings.
Similar to Peace Lily; reliable bloomer in low-light conditions.
Compact elegant palm for low-light rooms. Keep soil evenly moist.
Graceful arching palm; tolerates lower light than most palms.
Feathery golden cane palm; good air humidifier. Keep soil moist in summer.
Large silver-green striped leaves. Moves leaves up and down with the light cycle.
Striking burgundy undersides; needs filtered water and high humidity.
Prayer plant; folds leaves upward at night. Needs consistent moisture and no direct sun.
Purple clover-like leaves that close at night. Dormancy period in summer.
Swollen trunk stores water; very drought-tolerant. Not a true palm.
Striking architectural plant; allow soil to dry fully between waterings.
Extremely tolerant of neglect, low light, and irregular watering. Lives up to its name.
Classic trailing vine; likes cool temperatures and moist soil.
Fast-growing trailing plant with scalloped leaves; very easy to propagate.
Silvery-purple striped trailing leaves; grows quickly and roots easily in water.
Compact flowering plant; water from below to avoid leaf spots.
Waxy red spathes; avoid waterlogged soil and direct sun.
Broad crinkly fronds; keep moisture in the rosette centre and away from direct sun.
Epiphytic fern mounted on boards; soak the mounting base thoroughly then let dry.
Delicate fan-shaped leaflets; demands consistently moist soil and high humidity.
Vivid leaf veining; very sensitive to drying out and thrives in terrariums.
Explosively coloured foliage; needs bright light to maintain colour. Drops leaves if moved.
Umbrella-like leaf clusters; let the top layer of soil dry before watering.
Classic office tree; notorious for dropping leaves when moved or overwatered.
Soft-needled indoor tree; needs high humidity and bright light. Keep evenly moist.
Marginal aquatic; keep the pot standing in a saucer of water at all times.
Braided trunk with palmate leaves. Water thoroughly; allow to partially dry between waterings.
Usually grown in water; change water every 7–10 days or keep soil barely moist.
Clumping palm for low-light interiors; keep soil consistently moist.
Compact succulent with white horizontal stripes; tolerates lower light than most succulents.
Rosette-forming succulent; needs bright light and very free-draining soil.
Hens-and-chicks; extremely hardy rosette succulent, tolerates frost.
Classic spherical cactus; water sparingly in summer, almost never in winter.
Epiphytic cactus; water more frequently than desert cacti. Needs cool nights to bloom.
Most popular indoor orchid; water by soaking roots weekly, allow to drain fully.
Keep the central cup filled with water; flush occasionally to prevent stagnation.
Epiphyte needing no soil; mist 2–3 times a week or soak for 20 min weekly.
Coin-shaped leaves on a slender stem; let soil dry slightly between waterings.
Glossy cupped leaves; stores water in thick leaves so forgives missed waterings.
Striped leaves resembling watermelon rind; compact and undemanding.
Deeply textured dark green leaves; water when the top soil is dry.
Waxy thick-leaved vine producing fragrant porcelain-like flowers; let dry between waterings.
Heart-shaped succulent leaves; extremely slow-growing, very drought-tolerant.
Delicate trailing vine with tiny heart-shaped leaves; semi-succulent, let dry between waterings.
Tiny round leaves with turtle-shell patterning; needs well-draining soil.
Swiss-cheese vine with large perforated leaves; likes to climb and trail.
Yellow-green variegated heartleaf philodendron; easy trailing or climbing plant.
White pinstriped leaves on an upright plant; a recent hybrid that stays compact.
Classic golden variegated pothos; excellent for beginners.
Heavily white-marbled leaves; needs slightly more light than green pothos to maintain variegation.
Bright chartreuse-yellow leaves; same easy care as standard pothos.
Strap-like leaves with yellow stripe; one of the most common office plants.
Vivid green-and-yellow striped leaves; avoid fluoride in water.
Dark arrow-shaped leaves with dramatic white veins; needs humidity and consistent moisture.
Zebra-striped petioles; keep evenly moist and protect from cold draughts.
Papery coloured leaves in reds, pinks and whites; goes dormant in winter.
Large patterned tropical leaves; sap is irritating — wear gloves when handling.
Herringbone-patterned leaves; related to Calathea, similar humidity needs.
Tricolour pink-white-green leaves with magenta undersides; needs humidity.
Cheerful flowering windowsill plant; water when top cm of soil is dry.
Spectacular foliage in metallics and purples; keep humidity high and avoid stem rot.
Compact flowering begonia; prolific bloomer in bright indirect light.
Winter-flowering; water from below and keep cool (12–15 °C) for longest blooms.
Classic winter plant; keep out of draughts and water when soil surface is dry.
Intensely fragrant climbing plant; keep cool and bright to encourage flowering.
Fragrant Mediterranean shrub; needs maximum sun and excellent drainage indoors.
Woody culinary herb; needs full sun and free-draining soil. Mist occasionally.
Popular culinary herb; keep warm, bright and consistently moist. Pinch flowers to extend life.
Vigorous spreading herb; keep consistently moist and contain in a pot to stop spreading.
Easy windowsill herb; water when top soil is dry and snip regularly to encourage growth.
Dwarf lemon; needs maximum light, citrus feed, and consistent moisture. Cool winter rest helps flowering.
Drought-tolerant once established; needs full sun and sharp drainage. Move outside in summer.
Classic indoor bonsai; water when the surface is dry, mist leaves frequently.
Outdoor-preferred bonsai; if kept inside needs very bright light and cool winters.
Folds its leaves when touched; keep consistently moist and in bright indirect light.
Carnivorous plant; use distilled or rainwater only, keep in standing water and full sun.
Carnivorous sticky-tentacled plant; like the Venus flytrap, use only distilled water.
Tubular carnivorous plant; keep in a tray of distilled water and full sun.
Vivid pink-and-white variegated leaves; easy trailing plant, water when top soil is dry.
Develops fenestrated leaves with age when given a moss pole to climb.
Jungle cactus with cascading pencil-thin stems; more moisture-loving than desert cacti.
Trailing succulent with plump blue-green leaves; extremely fragile — avoid moving.
Bold white-veined leaves and yellow flower bracts; needs warmth, humidity and consistent moisture.
Bromeliad with a pink torch flower; keep cup filled with water, mist regularly.
